Yamamoto_intent: Preserve the fleet until an amphibious commitment fixes US operational geometry; improve reaction time and warning, but do not chase shaping raids or Majuro itself.

five_carrier_core.Taiho_integration: A-/A for normal first-cycle fleet operation; repeat-cycle/night/adverse-weather resilience now close to core standard but not assumed identical under battle damage.

secondary_carrier_pool.use: qualification/replacement/rear CAP/ferry plus contingency second-line battle support; not automatically merged into the five fast-core strike cycle.

Sulu_ASW_and_training.state: Improved Tokai/MAD + routine patrol + escorts keep training possible but not safe. US submarines still force zigzag, exercise cancellations and tanker/escort friction.
Sulu_ASW_and_training.late_24May_Tatekawa_audit: Historical Gurnard attack is not copied as a clean sinking. Centerline: Tatekawa Maru is torpedo-damaged/campaign-out and reaches/receives assistance near Davao; some fuel handling capacity is lost for roughly 2-3 weeks, but the tanker is not written off. This pays submarine risk without erasing the branch ASW improvement.
Sulu_ASW_and_training.training_result: Five-core deck flying continues on reduced/rotated days instead of the historical near-total curtailment.

Marianas_land_air_5Jun.note: This is a pre-US-strike state, not the 11 Jun battle result. Reinforcement is accelerated by persistent CRITICAL warning, but dispersal, maintenance and convoy/air-transfer friction prevent counting every assigned airframe as ready.

ISR: Marianas remains CRITICAL/PERSISTENT. Pickets/submarines/recon are weighted toward finding the US sortie rather than generating an offensive Majuro carrier hunt.
